speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: That specific location near the medial tibia sounds concerning for osteochondritis dissecans or a tibial tubercle stress injury. Given your recent increase in physical activity, have you noticed any swelling, locking, or a specific popping sound when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the update; the combination of PCOS, recent increased volleyball activity, and localized medial tibial pain raises suspicion for Osgood-Schlatter disease or tibial tubercle apophysitis. To confirm the extent of the injury, do you feel any tenderness directly over the tibial tubercle when I press, and have you noticed any visible swelling or a bony lump there? REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_Anteroposterior_XRay, Knee_Lateral_XRay

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, recent injuries, swelling or discoloration of the knee, or previous similar complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That's helpful; the lack of systemic symptoms like fever makes an infection unlikely. Since you have no swelling but report pain specifically over the tibial tubercle after starting volleyball, have you experienced any tenderness when you touch that specific bony bump?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter Disease (Tibial Tubercle Apophysitis)
